status: Concrete reuse/task proposal; no mapping upgrades or associations in this document checkpoint.
scope: A1.1/A1.3/A3.2/A3.4 traditions, local diversity and comparison; own/peer/local conditions remain actual application.

cases.facts: The organizer dates the Toronto initiative to 1967. The dated July 2020 Metrolinx account describes virtual cultural programming replacing the usual in-person parade because of COVID-19 circumstances, including a participant’s particular account of what the event meant to her.
cases.limits: Distinguish announced programming and participant experience from proof every planned event happened. The article’s prediction about 2021 is not an outcome. No claim every Caribbean family participates, every practice stopped, or technology caused the pandemic. Do not collapse current Carnival management and the original Caribana organization into one institution.

cases.facts: Nipissing First Nation’s 2026 announcement presents its annual Dewegigewaad, with drums, dance, craft and food activities.
cases.limits: A dated community-authored programme supports description of the particular celebration; it does not establish every family’s attendance or identical practices among Nations. Learn about publicly described activities; do not require performing ceremonies, imitation of sacred items or enrolment.

cases.facts: Retain the particular Kathy Morgan family conversations/gatherings and the council attribution already reviewed in the heritage dossier.
cases.limits: The non-Indigenous interviewer remains separately attributed. This particular family account is not sufficient alone to explain all local community changes, or the pupil’s own family/identity.

cases.facts: The organizers’ records distinguish 2020 in-person community lantern workshops/installation from 2021 virtual celebration and virtual workshops with outdoor art, explicitly connected to the pandemic. The artists’ project accounts report the installations and workshops, beyond the event announcements.
cases.limits: Compare the particular Toronto Chinatown programmes, not every Chinese household or all people celebrating Lunar New Year. Not every activity moved online: outdoor artworks remained, and the proposed scavenger hunt was postponed. Health guidance is historical2021 context, not current advice. No art reproduction or ritual performance required.

protocols.materials: Adult-prepared non-sensitive authentic accounts, pictures or objects concerning an ordinary shared family practice across generations. A birthday, annual meal or other willingly chosen practice can avoid religious or migration disclosure. The preparation protocol needs an actual supported reason for a change, not just dates. If no suitable own-family materials are available, record that local resource condition instead of claiming a fictional family satisfies it.
protocols.task: Identify a practice in the pupil’s family across multiple generations, compare what remained and what changed, and explain a principal reason supported by the account. A communication example may compare how relatives share the occasion across distance, but distinguish the reason for needing change from the tool that enabled it.
protocols.positive: Uses actual own-family evidence for a specific continuity/change and a supported reason; does not assume every tradition changes.
protocols.nearMiss: Names an old and new technology but never connects it to the chosen family practice, or invents an immigration/colonial cause.
protocols.transfer: Another aspect or generation of the chosen actual family practice, using a different source.
protocols.wholeClaimLimits: ChildhoodThenNow supplies continuity/change; TechnologyChanges contributes only where communication/home/travel change is actually relevant, not every reason for cultural change. No new general theory is inferred.

protocols.materials: Two verified Toronto worked cases: Caribbean Carnival before/2020 virtual format and Chinatown Lunar New Year 2020/2021 programmes, with dated organizer/participant sources and supported reasons. If the pupil’s local community is elsewhere, adult preparation supplies two actual local group cases with equivalent before/after evidence; Toronto is not relabelled as local.
protocols.task: Compare selected past/present practices for each group, identify a supported reason and distinguish continuity, changed format and lost/reclaimed practice.
protocols.positive: Uses source-supported changes/reasons across various actual local groups without treating one cause as universal.
protocols.nearMiss: Counts how many cultural words appear in the sources, generalizes one festival to all residents, or gives only one local group.
protocols.transfer: Another adult-verified local practice or changed circumstance while retaining correct attribution.
protocols.remainingBeforeFull: Exact task/contribution peer review and association qualification; the second Toronto case is now verified. CanadianRenewal remains specific and is not needed to invent a general cause for these cases.

protocols.materials: Adult-verified actual local groups and attributed public expressions. Toronto worked examples can include the council’s Métis gathering/family account and Caribbean Carnival. If the pupil’s community is elsewhere, substitute actual local evidence rather than relabel the Toronto case.
protocols.task: Identify several actual groups present locally and describe particular visible/audible community expressions using the evidence. Distinguish a community’s practices from assumptions about every individual.
protocols.positive: Names actual local groups and evidenced expressions with respectful, precise language.
protocols.nearMiss: Lists generic countries/foods without evidence of the local group or assigns identity from appearance.
protocols.transfer: Another verified local expression while retaining source and individual/community distinction.
protocols.wholeClaimLimits: SimilaritiesAndDifferences supplies respectful comparison; peoples recognition and vocabulary support particular aspects, not independent local knowledge without the packet.

protocols.materials: A voluntarily selected actual family practice, a peer’s actual or teacher-prepared attributed peer account, local community evidence, and the Nipissing First Nation programme as a particular other-Canadian-community case. A public source replaces neither the own-family nor peer condition.
protocols.task: Describe what is significant about selected practices and how people mark them across family, peer, local and another Canadian community, explicitly including the attributed First Nation example. Explain that commemoration and celebration need not have the same mood or purpose.
protocols.positive: Describes concrete practices across the required settings with attribution and respectful similarities/differences.
protocols.nearMiss: Only names holidays, omits peers/own community or assumes a fictional generic Indigenous festival meets the qualifier.
protocols.transfer: A different locally verified practice and representation, distinguishing what is known from the account from what is unknown.
protocols.wholeClaimLimits: CelebrationsWeShare remains grounded in actual shared family/peer practice; distant facts are source-specific extensions to the task, not proof of every pupil’s whole claim.

protocols.sourceInterpretation: The actual clause allows significant places and/or countries, and globe and/or maps. A worldwide-country requirement must not be added to every pupil’s task.
protocols.materials: An actual familiar public place meaningful to the pupil/family, such as a selected library, school or park, and an adult-verified map locating it. No home address, ancestry/migration disclosure or compulsory family tree is required. If a country is genuinely selected, use the actual broader map/globe and verify that location instead.
protocols.task: Identify chosen places and explain their actual personal/familial significance; locate the chosen places on the appropriate map, using its labels/key/reference. Also create/explain a familiar-place map with landmarks/key/relative locations where assessing the full existing map operation. Do not pretend a fictional or teacher-assigned location is personally significant.
protocols.positive: Connects actual significance to the correctly located place; distinguishes a familiar local place from a country if both are selected.
protocols.nearMiss: Names a place but cannot locate it, or locates a teacher-assigned foreign country without personal/familial significance.
protocols.transfer: Another genuinely meaningful public place or a different appropriate representation; a country path needs new verified geographic facts.
protocols.wholeClaimLimits: SpecialPlaces directly covers significance/features; FamiliarMaps covers the local representation operation. FamilyOrigins is only an optional relationship/origin component where relevant; no whole-family attainment is inferred from another person’s story.
protocols.remainingBeforeFull: Final source-fit review and exact contribution/association qualification; no universal global-location residual remains.

protocols.materials: Prepare actual non-sensitive own-family tradition accounts from more than one time/generation and an actual local-community practice with dated before/after evidence; supplied authentic sources are allowed. Public worked cases demonstrate how to use sources but replace neither the own-family nor local-community condition. Select only willingly shareable details, without collecting home addresses or unrelated family history.
task: Formulate questions about continuity/change in a chosen actual family practice and an actual community practice; link each question to the evidence needed, building on the earlier own-community question protocol.

Gather supplied primary/secondary materials with who/when/what information; distinguish a planned event announcement from evidence of the actual activity. Organize dated facts, noting an unknown as unknown rather than assuming an unmentioned practice did not happen.

Analyse and create a simple map with a key/labels showing actual public local celebration/practice locations and relative landmarks, then explain how those locations help answer the inquiry. A supplied schematic may support preparation but cannot be relabelled as the pupil’s actual community.

Use a dated timeline, like-for-like comparison table and meaningful same/changed classification or Venn diagram to identify continuity/change. Compare actual actions/materials/locations/formats from matched accounts; do not count source mentions or force an irrelevant bar chart. If a quantitative question is chosen, use actual comparable event/item records and state unit/coverage.

Evaluate which source supports each conclusion, identify a source limit and answer the original question. Announcements show plans; retrospective organizer/project accounts and appropriate family testimony can support what happened, with their own limits. A missing source entry is not proof a whole culture abandoned a practice.

Present the findings using source-attributed oral/written explanation plus map and other suitable representation, with clear tradition/generation/culture vocabulary. Include a cautious source-supported prediction for a changed circumstance and a method improvement, such as another relevant dated account, without predicting every family’s response.
protocols.positive: A coherent question–source–map/display–evaluation–conclusion–communication chain uses both actual own-family and local-community evidence and identifies continuity/change without inventing a cause.
protocols.nearMiss: A polished generic festival report lacks actual family/local application, a decorative chart counts vocabulary, or a prediction/announcement is described as an observed event.
protocols.transfer: Another willingly selected actual family/community practice or different source type; identify which inquiry steps transfer and which facts require fresh evidence.
protocols.wholeClaimLimits: Questions, shared research, surviving evidence, chronology, familiar maps and relevant displays each contribute their exact operation. DrawingConclusions is general enquiries despite its experiment example; the protocol includes report, supported conclusion, prediction and method improvement. No later broad historical-sourcing claim is given an unsupported younger context.
protocols.remainingBeforeFull: Final exact source/contribution review and scoped association qualification; the existing A2.1 Full question protocol is preserved unless this integrated protocol is selected explicitly.

consumerBoundary: Source-fit authoring design, not pupil attainment or a requirement to collect private family records. No new topic, DB action or learner-state transfer. Existing cases do not certify every local adaptation.
